newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU expansion would open export markets - Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: EU expansion would open export markets - Kinkel.

text.p: Eastward expansion would be the European Union's next strategic challenge after launching a single currency, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Tuesday.

The EU should not fear losing jobs to lower-wage neighbours because expansion would open up great export opportunities, Kinkel said in a written reply to a request for information by the opposition Social Democrats (SPD).
"The economic opening to the east is no job killer, but rather a strong motor for our export economy," he said.
Germany's trade with eastern Europe was comparable to the level of trade with the United States, and would double by 2000, he said.

Although entry candidates like the Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary must make themselves fiscally fit, the EU had a responsibility to add partners in the east after encouraging them to give up communism and join the west.
"For decades we have said, 'Come to us and build a common Europe.' This is a question of our credibility. We stand by our word," he said.

Germany, because of its extensive engagement in eastern Europe, was ready to serve as solicitor for entry candidates, said Kinkel, who also recommended a standing advisory conference of all current and future EU members.
